title: Reproducing Kao et al. 1988: wet oxidation of convex and concave silicon cylinders

sample.paper: (100) wafer; “The orientation of the vertical surface of a circular structure on a (100) wafer varies periodically from (100) to (110) around the periphery” (Part I); doping and resistivity of the cylinder wafers not stated
sample.ours: FAMILY: Si_Nanowire; ORIENTATION: Si100; DOPING: not_stated_undoped (recorded)
sample.note: The radial program has one rate around the circumference.

sample.paper: Silicon pillars etched 3 µm deep; “The smallest cylinder observed has a radius of approximately 1200 A”; radii “as measured from the SEM micrographs … the radii of the silicon surfaces after oxidation”
sample.ours: SHAPE: nanowire; DIAMETER_NM computed from the radius after oxidation and the oxide; RADIUS_AFTER_NM recorded; HEIGHT_NM 3000
sample.note: The etched radius is not given. It is back-computed with the program's volume ratio from the measured oxide, so it depends on the number scored. The program is an infinite cylinder; Kao measured at mid-height of a 3 µm pillar.

sample.paper: “on the left is a hole etched in the silicon with oxide grown on its inner (concave) surface”
sample.note: The radial program is convex only. A hole needs the opposite sign of the diffusion term and of the bulk pressure (Kao's Eqs. 8, 37–40).

sample.paper: “all oxide thicknesses are measured along the <110> surface, and the crystal orientation effect is neglected”
sample.note: Flat (110) grows 1.03 to 1.29 times flat (100) in steam (Part I Table 1).

sample.item: Flat reference of the same run
sample.paper: Thickness “normalized to the oxide thickness on the flat (100) vertical wall, which was calibrated to the oxide thickness on the (100) wafer surface” (Part I); Table 1 gives 457.5 to 555.4 nm
sample.note: The radial program reads it as a linear rate and then applies its own diffusion term, so as stated its flat sidewall grows only about 70% of it (see the alignment).

history.item: Circles and holes on the mask (smallest 1 um), AZ1470 resist, 4:1 projection aligner
history.paper: “Positive photoresist AZ1470 was patterned by ultraviolet light, using a Canon FPA-141F 4:1 projection aligner.”
history.ours: SHAPE and the diameter on the sample
history.note: Part I: small dots came out smaller and holes larger than drawn; the as-etched radius is not reported.

history.item: Anisotropic plasma etch to 3 um, SF6 + chlorofluorocarbon, about 6.5 min per um
history.paper: “The structures were etched to a depth of 3 um”; “The etching rate of the silicon substrate was approximately 6.5 min for 1 pm”
history.ours: SHAPE and the diameter on the sample; HEIGHT_NM 3000 recorded

history.item: RCA clean ending in 50:1 HF, 30 s, and a rinse
history.paper: “5:1:1 H2O:H2O2:NH4OH at 70°C, 10 min … 5:1:1 H2O:H2O2:HCl at 70°C, 10 min … 50:1 HF for 30 sec”
history.ours: CLEAN: peroxide_HF on the sample; no program reads it
RUN PushIn DURATION 600 TEMP 700->800 AMBIENT inert_N2
history.note: Neither paper describes the furnace cycle. 10 min from 700 °C in nitrogen is ours.

history.paper: “Table 1: CONDITIONS FOR WET PLANAR OXIDATION … Time(min) 1440 300 96 40 24” (Part I); “after sufficient time has elapsed for each temperature such that the flat surface has grown approximately 5000 Å of oxide” (PDF p. 10)
history.ours: RUN WetOxidation DURATION 86400 TEMP 800->800 AMBIENT steam
history.note: How the steam was made (pyrogenic or bubbler) and its pressure are not stated; pure steam at 1 atm is ours. The radial program takes its rate from the run's flat oxide, so the steam pressure does not enter.

history.ours: RUN PullOut DURATION 600 TEMP 800->700 AMBIENT inert_N2
history.note: 10 min to 700 °C in nitrogen is ours.

history.paper: “As a protective layer over the oxide, a 1 pm LPCVD polysilicon was deposited at 620*C and at a pressure of 500 mTorr for 90 min.”
history.ours: recorded, not simulated: the language has no deposition ambient
history.note: 90 min at 620 °C after the oxidation. No program here grows oxide in it; at Kao's viscosities (above 10^15 P below 800 °C) the oxide's stress would not relax in 90 min either.

history.paper: “The failure to identify a suitable etching process led to the apparently imprecise procedure of mechanical lapping.”
history.note: Depth varies by up to 1 um over 3 mm; the patterns were clustered in 2 × 3 mm to limit it.

history.item: Oxide etched out in 6:1 buffered HF, 100 Å gold sputtered
history.paper: “The lapped samples were first immersed in 6:1 buffered HF for several minutes to etch out the oxide, and a 100 layer of gold was then sputtered”
history.note: The SEM measures the gap the oxide leaves.

history.item: SEM, x20,000 to x50,000: oxide on the (110) part of the wall, and the silicon radius after oxidation
history.paper: “the characterization of retarded oxidation was based on oxide thicknesses measured on the (110) surface and normalized to the oxide thickness on the flat (100) vertical wall”; “the radii in all plots are as measured from the SEM micrographs, they represent the radii of the silicon surfaces after oxidation”
history.ours: the observable Thickness; the radius after oxidation is Core_diameter / 2

history.paper: k_s = k_0 exp{−σ_rr(Ω_SiO2 − Ω_Si)/kT} (Eq. 41); C* = C*_0 exp{−P V_s/kT} (Eq. 43); η = η_0 exp{αP} (Eq. 44); D's stress dependence (Eq. 42) “was not included in this numerical implementation”; Table I: η_0 = 1.0e15, 3.0e14, 3.0e13, 6.0e12, 6.0e11 P and α = 7.5e-11, 2.0e-10, 5.0e-10, 6.0e-10, 6.0e-10 cm²/dyne at 800 to 1200 °C, V_s = 7.5 Å³; ΔΩ = 25 Å³ fixed
history.ours: the radial program's stress form: exp(−stress) on the reaction with stress = stress_time × (1 − 0.44) × a × growth × (1/a² − 1/b²), one stress_time (142 s, fitted on Müller), no solubility or viscosity pressure terms, no temperature
history.note: stress_time is 2η ΔΩ/kT in Kao's terms. Kao's Table I gives 3.4 × 10⁵ s at 800 °C and 148 s at 1200 °C; Müller's fit, 142 s at 850 °C, is Kao's 1200 °C viscosity.

history.paper: “The stress-free values of the parameters (k_0, D_0, and C*_0) are as specified in the Deal-Grove model”
history.ours: the run's flat oxide over its steam time as the linear rate; A = 1.1 µm (Deal and Grove, 850 °C) at every temperature
history.note: The program has no temperature: A is the 850 °C value at 800 to 1200 °C.

cases.label: Convex cylinder, wet 800 °C, radius 500 nm after oxidation
cases.note: Normalized oxide 0.73 read from Kao's least-squares line in Part I Figure 7 at 1/r = 2 per µm; times the flat (100) oxide of Table 1, 502.7 nm. The etched diameter 1373 nm is computed from the radius after oxidation and this oxide.
